text.title: 柠檬酸是否改变挥发酸与质量评分的关系？
text.question: 在红、白葡萄酒各自内部，控制其他已测理化变量后，volatile_acidity 与 quality 的关联是否随 citric_acid 水平而改变？

core.object: 单个葡萄酒样本的测量化学特征与质量评分
core.relation_or_action: citric_acid 对 volatile_acidity–quality 条件关联的调节
core.contrast: 在较低与较高 citric_acid 水平下，volatile_acidity 与 quality 的调整后关联
core.prediction: 事前预测在至少一种颜色中，较高 citric_acid 会减弱 volatile_acidity 与 quality 的负向关联；若共同支持范围内的交互接近零或方向相反，则该预测不获支持。
core.independent_unit: 单个样本；生产批次、酒庄和评审依赖关系未知。

text.failure_condition: 在颜色内共同支持范围和合理的序数模型规格下，交互接近零或方向不稳定。
assumptions: quality 是序数感官评分，不等同消费者偏好。
citric_acid 只是已测化学指标，不直接测量感知酸度或缓冲能力。
观察性关联不识别调配或发酵干预效果。
text.required_new_data: 当前数据可检验条件关联。若要检验干预效果，需要按颜色制作独立酒批次，在控制其他条件下操纵两种酸相关成分，并由盲法评审重复评分。
text.domain_value: 可判断挥发酸与评分的关系是否依赖另一种酸相关成分，从而为后续盲法感官实验提供具体交互假设；不会单凭现有数据导出酿造建议。

text.title: Does free sulfur dioxide add information beyond total concentration and pH?
text.question: Within red and white samples separately, is the free sulfur dioxide concentration associated with quality after accounting flexibly for total sulfur dioxide, pH, and the other measured chemistry, and does that conditional association differ by color?

core.object: Wine sample quality scores and free and total sulfur dioxide measurements
core.relation_or_action: Compare ordinal models with flexible total sulfur dioxide and pH terms, with and without free sulfur dioxide and its interaction with color
core.contrast: Conditional quality association of free sulfur dioxide at comparable total sulfur dioxide and pH, across colors
core.prediction: Free sulfur dioxide will add a nonzero, color-dependent association beyond total concentration and pH.

text.failure_condition: The added terms do not improve held-out within-color ordinal fit or estimates are unstable in regions with joint support.
assumptions: The two measurements are comparable across samples.
The observational association is not interpreted as the effect of changing sulfur dioxide.
Measured chemistry does not eliminate unmeasured production or lot confounding.
text.required_new_data: None for the observational comparison; production recommendations require prospective controlled cellar measurements and sensory evaluation.
text.domain_value: Tests whether the free concentration carries information beyond total concentration and acidity, rather than assuming that a derived fraction has a clear sensory meaning.

text.title: 相对排序一致与评分差异来源
text.idea: 评委对酒样的相对顺序是否一致；评委严厉度、酒样差异及评委与酒样交互分别怎样影响评分？
text.motivation: 排序一致和绝对分数一致是不同目标；只补无身份个体分数仍不能把差异归因到评委、酒样或交互。

text.title: 既定评审流程的聚合分预测
text.idea: 对既定葡萄酒评审流程产生的 quality 中位数，理化测量与聚合分之间的关系是什么；它与个体评委分数层面的关系是否相同？
text.motivation: 现表直接给出聚合中位数；预测这一输出与解释评委分歧或感官机制不是同一个主张。

text.title: Does residual sugar modify the alcohol–quality association within wine color?
text.question: Within red and white wines separately, is the association between alcohol and sensory quality more positive at higher residual sugar, after accounting for the other measured physicochemical variables and restricting comparisons to overlapping composition ranges?

core.object: Row-level quality scores and physicochemical measurements for red and white vinho verde samples
core.relation_or_action: Estimate alcohol-by-residual-sugar interaction in an ordinal quality model, with color-specific terms and adjustment for the other measured chemistry
core.contrast: Alcohol–quality slope at higher versus lower residual sugar within each color, compared with a model lacking the interaction
core.prediction: The alcohol–quality association will be more positive at higher residual sugar in at least one color; this is an observational prediction, not a sugar intervention effect
core.independent_unit: Wine sample row; whether rows represent independent lots is unknown

text.failure_condition: The interaction is negligible or inconsistent across colors, lacks support within common composition ranges, or disappears under reasonable model and influence checks.
assumptions: The quality score has an ordinal interpretation.
Measured covariates and common-support restriction address only measured composition; unmeasured style and producer effects may remain.
A row is a suitable analysis unit, though independence across rows is unverified.
text.required_new_data: None for an observational test. Causal interpretation would require randomized sugar and alcohol manipulations with blinded panel ratings.
text.domain_value: A reproducible interaction could motivate testing whether composition-specific sensory guidance differs by wine style; a null result would discourage treating a pooled alcohol association as a balance rule.

text.title: 评委绝对评分一致
text.idea: 若实际用途要求不同评委的绝对评分可互换，评委对同一酒样是否给出相近分数？
text.motivation: 中位数丢失个体分布，不能由聚合值估计评委间绝对差异；该目标不同于预测中位数。

text.title: 聚合评分的潜在感官构念效度
text.idea: 评审流程给出的评分是否测量了一个独立定义的潜在感官属性？
text.motivation: 可靠或一致的评分不自动证明构念效度；中位数也不能仅凭自身成为无误差的潜在感官真值。

text.title: Does visible wine color shift ratings of the same wine?
text.question: For the same wine samples, does showing versus masking visual color change blinded panelists’ ordinal quality ratings, and does that within-sample effect differ between red and white wines?

core.object: Repeated panelist ratings of the same wine samples under visible-color and opaque-glass conditions
core.relation_or_action: Randomize serving condition within panelist and sample, then estimate the visibility effect and its interaction with wine color
core.contrast: Visible-color versus masked-color rating for the same sample, compared across red and white wines
core.prediction: Visible color will shift ratings for at least one wine color relative to masked presentation.
core.independent_unit: Panelist-by-sample pair for the within-pair contrast, with repeated measurements clustered by panelist and wine sample

text.failure_condition: The within-sample visibility effect is negligible in both wine colors, with uncertainty excluding a prespecified practically meaningful rating shift.
assumptions: Serving order is randomized and panelists are blinded to the study hypothesis.
Opaque and visible conditions differ primarily in visual information, not temperature, aroma access, or serving procedure.
Analysis accounts for repeated ratings by both panelist and sample.
text.required_new_data: A panel study using the same red and white samples served in randomized visible and opaque conditions, with panelist and sample identifiers and repeated ordinal ratings.
text.domain_value: Would test whether visual appearance contributes to the sensory score independently of the measured chemistry, helping interpret what the dataset’s quality ratings represent.

text.title: Do chemical associations shift every adjacent quality threshold in the same way?
text.question: Within each wine color, does a common latent ordinal model adequately describe how the 11 measured chemical variables relate to quality, or do particular variables have materially different associations at different adjacent quality-score thresholds?

core.object: Observed integer quality score for one wine sample
core.relation_or_action: Association between measured chemistry and crossing adjacent quality-score thresholds
core.contrast: A proportional-odds model with common chemistry slopes versus a partial proportional-odds model allowing prespecified threshold-specific slopes
core.prediction: Most chemistry slopes will be directionally consistent across thresholds, but at least one will vary materially across thresholds in one or both colors.
core.independent_unit: One wine row; producer, lot, and panelist clustering are unknown.

text.failure_condition: Threshold-specific slopes do not improve prespecified held-out ordinal log loss beyond uncertainty, or their apparent differences are unstable across color and resampling.
assumptions: The integer score is an ordered outcome, though equal numeric spacing is not assumed.
The available chemistry measures have adequate support across adjacent score categories within color.
Row-based resampling is exploratory because sampling clusters are unavailable.
text.required_new_data: For confirmation of score-generation differences, independently sampled wines with lot identifiers and repeated blinded ratings from a shared panel.
text.domain_value: Shows whether a single sensory ordering can summarize chemistry-score associations or whether particular score transitions warrant separate sensory or process investigation.

text.title: How much quality disagreement remains among chemically similar wines?
text.question: Within each color, do wines with very similar measured physicochemical profiles have more similar quality scores than expected under a quality-label permutation that preserves color and coarse chemistry strata?

core.object: Quality-score disagreement among same-color wine pairs
core.relation_or_action: Relate multivariate physicochemical distance to absolute quality-score difference
core.contrast: Observed disagreement among prespecified nearest-neighbor pairs versus a conditional permutation reference
core.prediction: Nearest-neighbor pairs have smaller quality-score differences than the permutation reference, but nonzero disagreement remains.
core.independent_unit: A wine row; pairwise comparisons are dependent, and lot, producer, and panel identifiers are unavailable.

text.failure_condition: Nearest-neighbor pairs show no lower disagreement than the conditional permutation reference, or results change materially under reasonable distance and stratum definitions.
assumptions: Chemistry can be scaled comparably within color for distance calculations.
The permutation strata preserve relevant broad chemistry and score distributions.
Pair-level uncertainty accounts for shared rows; rows are not independent replicates of a sensory panel.
text.required_new_data: Independent wines with lot and producer identifiers, repeated blinded sensory ratings, and the same physicochemical measurements to separate sample variation from rating and batch variation.
text.domain_value: Tests whether measured chemistry is locally informative about sensory scores and identifies whether chemistry-similar samples still require additional sensory or process measurements.

text.title: Are quality scores reproducible across repeated blind ratings?
text.question: For wines spanning the observed quality range, does within-wine disagreement across repeated blinded ratings vary by score category, and is it greater near category transitions than for wines consistently rated within one category?

core.object: Repeated blinded ordinal ratings of the same wine sample
core.relation_or_action: Relate within-wine rating disagreement to the wine's rating distribution and category
core.contrast: Within-wine disagreement for samples whose ratings span adjacent categories versus samples whose ratings remain in one category
core.prediction: Ratings will disagree more often for samples whose repeat ratings straddle adjacent categories than for samples whose ratings remain in one category.
core.independent_unit: Wine sample, with repeated ratings nested within wine and panelist.

text.failure_condition: Category-straddling samples do not show greater within-wine disagreement, or the difference vanishes after accounting for panelist and session.
assumptions: The same samples can be presented repeatedly under blinded, randomized order.
Panelists and sessions are recorded so rating dependence can be modeled.
The supplied quality score does not reveal its replication or panel structure.
text.required_new_data: A set of independently sampled wines rated repeatedly by multiple blinded panelists across randomized sessions, with wine, panelist, and session identifiers.
text.domain_value: Separates stable sample-level score differences from rating variation and can identify categories where sensory assessment needs closer calibration.
